title: Paddington began on a shop shelf
hook: Paddington began as a lonely toy bear left on a London shop shelf.
peek: On Christmas Eve 1956, Michael Bond saw a small teddy bear sitting alone on a shelf in Selfridges in London. He bought it for his wife, named it after a nearby station, and soon started writing stories about it.
lede: On Christmas Eve 1956, Michael Bond, then a BBC cameraman, was in Selfridges department store in London. On a shelf he spotted a single small teddy bear left unsold. He felt sorry for it, bought it as a present for his wife Brenda, and named it Paddington after the station near their flat.

bullets.text: A while later, staring at a blank page, Bond looked at the bear and began writing about it. He said the first book, A Bear Called Paddington, took about ten days. It was published in 1958.

Paddington arrives at the station with a label reading "Please look after this bear. Thank you." Bond said this came from his memory of children evacuated from London during the war, carrying labels and small cases.
In Bond's first draft the bear came from darkest Africa. His agent pointed out that Africa has no native bears, so Bond changed it to darkest Peru, home of the spectacled bear.
Paddington keeps a marmalade sandwich under his hat in case of emergencies, a habit picked up from his Aunt Lucy. The books have sold tens of millions of copies and led to a series of hit films.
